ordered_diagnoses: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion

s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative skin lesion with erythema and nodules
salient_findings: Pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
Well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque over the right side of the anterior chest wall
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
key_facts: History of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
Underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by right modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiotherapy
Noticed skin lesion after radiotherapy
Lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
Presentation to dermatology 1 year after initial cancer diagnosis
Erythematous plaque measured 15 × 12 cm
Multiple palpable small nodules within the erythema
Immunohistochemistry negative for ER, PR, and HER2
Skin biopsy showed multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels

shortlist: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion

shortlist.label: Cutaneous metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and skin biopsy showing multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presentation of a well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque with multiple palpable small nodules, consistent with inflammatory breast carcinoma

shortlist.label: Carcinomatous lymphangitis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showing multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels, indicating lymphatic spread of breast cancer cells

shortlist.label: Lymphangitic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and skin biopsy results consistent with lymphatic invasion of breast cancer cells

shortlist.label: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer, clinical presentation, and skin biopsy results indicating cutaneous lymphatic invasion of breast cancer cells

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels, as seen in the skin biopsy, is a key finding that supports the diagnosis of carcinomatous lymphangitis, which is characterized by the invasion of cancer cells into lymphatic vessels.

rejected.label: Cutaneous metastasis
rejected.why: While cutaneous metastasis is a possibility, the specific finding of carcinoma cells in lymphatic vessels points more towards carcinomatous lymphangitis.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast carcinoma
rejected.why: Inflammatory breast carcinoma typically presents with rapid onset of erythema and edema of the breast, which is not the primary presentation in this case.

rejected.label: Lymphangitic carcinoma
rejected.why: Lymphangitic carcinoma is another term for carcinomatous lymphangitis, but the provided shortlist uses 'Carcinomatous lymphangitis' as the specific label.

rejected.label: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion
rejected.why: This option is less specific than carcinomatous lymphangitis, which directly describes the invasion of lymphatic vessels by cancer cells.
